newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mixed.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Friday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose sharply to 3.455 billion yuan from 1.785 billion yuan with the 60-day contract the most actively traded.
Trading was more active than Thursday due to a series of positive factors, traders said.
With the month-end approaching, financial institutions were required to do their monthly settlements, which boosted fund demand on the interbank market, traders said.

The announcement of a national state debt depository will help check irregularities on the state debt secondary market, making more institutions make use of the interbank market for short-term funds, they said.

In addition, the active domestic A share markets made more securities houses borrow money on the interbank market through the short-term financial centres, money brokerages run by the central bank. Two new A share issues on the Shanghai stock exchange also fueled fund demand.
"Non-banking financial institutions, in particular the securities houses, were the most active traders on Friday due to the active A share markets," said a trader.
Traders said trading volume on the interbank market was expected to stay at high levels with the rates moving narrowly. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
